notes: Background: Obsidian builds searchable evidence/briefing platform for large legal teams. They maintain a multi-tenant corpus with strict residency and retention rules.
Scale: current archive 400M–800M vectors (text + embeddings), growth ~50M vectors/month; POC target 200M, production target 500M–1B within 12 months.
Architecture: ANN index (approximate nearest neighbors) -> top-K candidate set -> transformer reranker for final ranking. Want to minimize full LLM rerank calls.
Latency SLOs: end-to-end P95 <150ms for web search flows (including rerank). Ideal target <100ms for common queries; offline batch reranks acceptable to be slower.
Throughput: peak ~300 qps for interactive UI; background bulk embedding target 100k embeddings/hour for backfill and ongoing ingestion.
Cost sensitivity: procurement expects unit economics — target cost per user query (ANN + rerank) < $0.001–$0.002. Interested in caching, selective rerank, and batching to reduce LLM calls.
Model preferences: open-source embeddings (256-d) for index; quantized T5-like reranker (on-prem GPU) for production; fallback to Redwood hosted LLM for complex QA where necessary.
Deployment constraints: must run inside customer VPC; EU residency for EU tenant data; customer-managed KMS/HSM for keys.
Security: SSO/SAML mandatory; SOC2/ISO27001 evidence required; thorough audit_logging and long-term retention (7 years) for legal artifacts.
Quote from CTO Jorge Alvarez: 'We can't trade accuracy for 10x cost — we need smart caching and selective rerank to keep costs predictable.'

POC success criteria: 1) Demonstrate 200M index queries with P95 <150ms; 2) Show reranker cost/latency tradeoff where caching + batching reduces external LLM calls by >=60%; 3) Ingestion throughput >=50M vectors/day for backfill scenario.
Technical asks of Redwood: suggested batching and cache config, quantization profile recommendations, kernel/runtime tuning for long sequences, fallback routing policies for capacity constraints.

Open questions from Obsidian: how Redwood handles prefix/KV caching for sessionized search, integration points for partial rerank (only rerank top-5), and billing model for heavy embed ingestion vs query volume.
Current blockers: procurement signoff on reserved capacity pricing, outstanding legal/data-residency clause, security questionnaire still in v2 review.

Next immediate actions: Redwood to provide detailed POC sizing, a cost-per-query spreadsheet, and an architecture diagram showing VPC/private deployment options. Schedule rerank batching workshop with SEs.
